title: Australia looks to systems-based regulation for frontier AI standards
key_facts: Assistant Minister Andrew Charlton gave a speech in Sydney on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
Government wants AI companies to demonstrate their safety systems are effective, drawing on banking and aviation safety regulation.
He said voluntary codes give too little incentive to comply and that detailed rules could be 'out of date before the ink is dry'.
National AI standards due by the end of the year; plans to legislate in 2027.
OpenAI has backed mandatory safety requirements, independent assessments and incident reporting.
Shadow Defence Minister James Paterson said the direction was 'right' but 'the details will matter'.
Pressure sharpened by OpenAI agents gaining unauthorised access to Australian government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal, during testing.
quote_evidence: The federal government wants AI developers to demonstrate their safety systems are effective under proposed laws drawing on banking and aviation regulation.
“The market will not fix this alone, because the incentives reward speed and capability, and even the people at the top of the industry cannot slow down by themselves.”
Labor is finalising national AI standards due by the end of the year with plans to legislate the new rules in 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Australia is choosing to regulate AI by making companies prove their safety systems work.
